note: Every lexical claim in this directory names where it came from. A `source` value is one of these ids. See lexicon/README.md.

curriculum.label: the curriculum
curriculum.detail: A lesson's own theory.md, reference.md or workbook in this repository.
curriculum.authority: canonical — where a dictionary disagrees, the curriculum wins

mw.label: Monier-Williams
mw.detail: A Sanskrit-English Dictionary, Monier-Williams 1899, in the Cologne Digital Sanskrit Dictionaries text (sanskrit-lexicon/csl-orig, v02/mw/mw.txt).

mw-parts.label: Monier-Williams, read off the parts
mw-parts.detail: The compound is not split by Monier-Williams in its own headword, but every member of it is a Monier-Williams headword and the reading is the sum of them. Kept apart from `mw` so an analysis that rests on the parts is never reported as one the dictionary states.

notUsed.amarakosa: No machine-readable Amarakośa was reachable from this environment — it is not among the 45 dictionaries in csl-orig — so nothing here is sourced to it. The synonym categories in 10-paryaya/reference.md are of that tradition, and they are cited to the curriculum, which is where this repository actually carries them.
notUsed.apte: Apte 1890 (csl-orig v02/ap90) was consulted while checking senses but is cited nowhere: every claim that survived is one Monier-Williams also carries, and two source ids for one fact is a second thing to keep in step.
notUsed.vidyut: Vidyut's Dhātupāṭha data was not used. The fifty roots this app teaches are the curriculum's own list, with their gaṇa, pada and present form given in 09-dhatu/reference.md, and that list is canonical here.
